review.reason:
Candidate 44 passes as supplied. The artwork maps confidently to the numbered connected routing and preserves the important hazard relationships without requiring geometry changes.

Hole 1: The 574-yard uphill par 5 runs from T1 across the lower property to G1 beside T2. Its single substantial lake remains on the player's right, extending along nearly the whole fairway. The two left-side fairway bunkers and back-right greenside cluster are retained. The generous landing corridor supports conservative three-shot play away from water, but the left-side sand complicates simply favoring that side on every shot. The illustration preserves the shoreline extent and credible fairway-to-green proportions.

Hole 2: The dry 305-yard split-fairway par 4 returns from T2 through the broad upper fairway toward G2 near T3. The central collision-tree island, its fairway bunker and alternative landing lanes are clearly recognizable in the artwork. Choosing a lane offers a controlled placement route, while attacking the green directly introduces tree and target-control risk. Greenside sand remains on both sides toward the back. The illustration consolidates some small bunker shapes without a clear side reversal. Its simulated one-shot reach indicates an attacking opportunity, not an automatically safe drive.

Hole 3: The dry 149-yard punchbowl par 3 plays from T3 down toward G3, passing the separate foreground landing patch. Its relatively large green and bilateral back-side bunker groups are faithfully retained. The open entrance and generous central target provide a conservative alternative to a precise pin attack. This is principally a short distance-control test, appropriately contrasting with the two longer holes.

The long shoreline par 5, short split-route par 4 and compact dry par 3 provide excellent within-round variety. Across-days novelty is sufficient rather than exceptional: all three types have appeared before, but the much shorter, dry punchbowl contrasts with course 103's wet 211-yard version, and the drivable split fairway differs materially from course 100's 429-yard hole. Safe tee-option counts of 59/121/44 and simulated 3/1/1 shots to green support fair difficulty; the visible landing spaces independently remain usable.

The 5:3 landscape artwork retains a compact irregular shared property, folded out-and-back routing, varied orientations and short green-to-next-tee connections. Selective groves leave grassy breaks, with continuous interior grass and white confined to the exterior. Each putting green reads as one natural apple-green surface with a narrow, restrained fringe, not a nested disc or raised platform. No clear hazard-side, lake-extent or proportion mismatch warrants an edit.
